subject.entry: D-001 — Definition of "completed" for the V2 design
subject.bindingNote: This verdict binds to the START bytes above. A coordinator work lane was active during review; HEAD moved 0ada5b3 -> 4cfd9d4 mid-review (evidence-identity-recipes v9 review REJECT and v10 landed in that commit). All non-subject measurements below record the digest actually read.

reviewer: adversarial-subagent (D-000 protocol; mandate: refute, not confirm)
protocol: D-000: adversarial review to consensus, 3 turns each side maximum, else CONTESTED-parked with both positions

objections.claim: D-001 §1 claims it adopts the five conditions 'verbatim and without amendment' but it paraphrases, and two of the paraphrases weaken the checklist.
objections.evidence: (a) Condition 3 in file 08 ends with the anti-loophole guard 'Merely receiving a rejecting disposition never satisfies this gate.' — D-001 drops the sentence entirely. (b) File 08 requires each rejecting finding 'individually identified, closed or lawfully routed to an owning authority/register item, and backed by retained evidence'; D-001 compresses to 'individually closed or lawfully routed with retained evidence', losing 'identified' and the owning-authority/register-item routing target. (c) File 08's DR-012 clause: 'it remains mandatory before release or authoritative launch'; D-001 renders it 'release-only', which read literally would let an authoritative launch that is not a 'release' escape DR-012. (d) Lesser rewordings ('that names'->'naming', 'have'->'carry', 'owners'->'named owners', dropping 'creation of') are individually harmless but jointly falsify the word 'verbatim'.
objections.proposedFix: Replace §1's restatement with a byte-exact quotation of file 08's 'Blueprint-readiness decision' section, or incorporate by reference to the section anchor plus the file digest 528cab56ae2459876a1c17a60c11681eaa3190849dc9c2ad3d253d31f1cfce8a and delete the paraphrase. If a paraphrase is kept, drop the word 'verbatim' and restore the condition-3 guard sentence and the full DR-012 clause.

objections.claim: The DR-006 route pins an artifact head that is already independently REJECTED; executing the route as written would promote a rejected candidate, exactly the promotion-without-review-then-apply the register prohibits.
objections.evidence: D-001 routes DR-006 as 'EIR v9 `d3e0d4c9…` review → acceptance → binding recipes'. Measured: evidence-identity-recipes.v9.json sha256 = d3e0d4c9491f46c0c71dcab10fa685b33c3736ef3651db0fcc232621868f1b22 (pin matches), but evidence-identity-recipes.v9.review-independent.json carries verdict REJECT, blockerCount 1; evidence-identity-recipes.v10.json (5ddbb180…) now exists as head with zero reviews on disk. Commit 4cfd9d4 ('evidence-identity-recipes.v10: repair B-EIR9-01; v9 review recorded') landed during this review. D-001 was synthesized at 0ada5b3 when v9 was the unreviewed head, so the route was coherent when drafted — and falsified one commit later, which is the point: a version-pinned route in a decision text goes stale before the decision can even be adopted.
objections.proposedFix: Route DR-006 by process over the current head, not by version: 'current EIR head → independent review → acceptance → apply', pinning the §7.1 PROPERTY (which D-001 already correctly names as the boundary) rather than a version number. Apply the same head-agnostic form to every §3 route that names a live candidate version.

objections.claim: The R04 route 'apply reviewed delivery.v5' contradicts the review it cites: that review accepts the artifact as a CANDIDATE and EXPRESSLY NOT FOR APPLICATION, with a standing disqualifier.
objections.evidence: delivery.v5.review-independent.json (1e5de421…) verdict opens: 'ACCEPT WITH NON-BLOCKING OBSERVATIONS — AS A CANDIDATE, AND EXPRESSLY NOT FOR APPLICATION.' and closes: 'THE SECTION 7.1 DISQUALIFIER STANDS AT FULL STRENGTH AND THIS VERDICT DOES NOT DISCHARGE IT: no instrument in this corpus reads these bytes, measured, and section 7.1 grades that disqualifying for application.' Treating candidate acceptance as an application warrant is the exact trap file 08's DR-002 acceptance note records: 'A PASSED with a DO-NOT-SEAL recommendation is not an application warrant.' D-001 marks only the OBS-1-retention half contestable; overriding the not-for-application condition is nowhere marked as a decision at all.
objections.proposedFix: Rewrite R04's route as: commission/review an instrument that reads the delivery.v5 bytes (discharging the §7.1 disqualifier), obtain an application-grade acceptance, then apply. If the coordinator intends to apply against the review's express condition, that is a separate PREFERENCE-LADEN decision requiring its own D-000 review — add it to §4 or drop it.

objections.claim: The DR-011 subledger is not fully routed: §3 names routes for 8 of 16 residuals (9 counting R16 via DR-010), leaves 7 unrouted, orphans R02 entirely, and drops half of R12's required closure.
objections.evidence: §3 condition 1 routes R03, R04, R05, R07, R10, R12, R13, R14 by name; R16 is reachable via DR-010's route. R01, R02, R06, R08, R09, R11, R15 appear nowhere. Some have plausible parent-row coverage (R06~DR-002..008 chain, R08~DR-007, R09~DR-009, R11~DR-005, R01/R15~DR-006) but D-001 never says so, and DR-011's own acceptance cell requires EVERY residual row individually CLOSED or LAWFULLY-DISPOSED. R02 (fact-identity-policy: checker states 13/14 implementable, capability property NOT DISCHARGED, corpus and imperative-authority parks) maps to no parent DR route in D-001 at all. R12's route ('individually-disposed 19+7+4') covers only the second half of the row; file 08 also requires 'V1-owned dual-head reconciliation' and separately 'The v8 claim-shape obligation must be reconciled separately' — neither appears in D-001.
objections.proposedFix: Route all 16 residuals by name. Where a residual closes through a parent DR row's route, say so explicitly per row. Add R02 a route of its own. Extend R12's route with the v8/v13 dual-head reconciliation as a distinct work item.

objections.claim: DR-108 is silently dropped from the condition-2 routing — the exact 'silence' D-001 forswears.
objections.evidence: §3 condition 2 partitions rows into product (DR-104/115/116/117/118/119/123/128/129), rule-governed architecture authoring (DR-101/102/103/105/107/110/111/112/114/120/121/122/125/126/127), and inherit-blocked (DR-106/109/113/124's evidence class): 28 rows accounted for out of the 29 in file 08's table. DR-108 (secret credential storage via keychain; 'Hard blocker only for features requiring stored credentials') appears in none of the three lists, while D-001 itself promises 'Items D-002 excludes get explicit deferral dispositions, never silence.' Also partial: only DR-124's 'evidence class' is classified; the rest of DR-124 is unrouted.
objections.proposedFix: Add DR-108 to the routing (rule-governed architecture authoring with review, or an explicit slice-conditional deferral once D-002 lands). State the route for the non-evidence-class remainder of DR-124.

objections.claim: Commit C4 batches two register-content decisions (a new DR row, a row widening) inside 'the one batched mechanical commit', breaking D-000 clause-4 per-decision revertibility and letting non-mechanical decisions bypass adversarial review under a 'mechanical' label.
objections.evidence: C4 = 'pin-move corrections, six verify-then-moves, V2TOPIC-F-01/F-02/F-04, vocabulary normalization — the one batched mechanical commit'. V2TOPIC-F-02 is 'a new DR row owning the V1→V2 transition contract' — authoring a new register row (its condition, owner, acceptance evidence) is a decision, not hygiene. V2TOPIC-F-04 widens DR-117 ('widened first per V2TOPIC-F-04') — changing a row's scope changes what condition 2 requires. Reverting either alone would require reverting the genuinely mechanical pin corrections with it; and a scope-widening decided as 'hygiene' escapes the D-000 review lane — the precise axis-3 failure mode D-001 claims to prevent.
objections.proposedFix: Split C4: keep pin-move corrections, verify-then-moves, F-01 (stale recital fix) and vocabulary normalization as the mechanical commit; land V2TOPIC-F-02 and F-04 as separate commits, each with its own D-000 adversarial review and register entry.

objections.claim: V2TOPIC-F-01/F-02/F-04 — cited as route inputs — exist nowhere in the corpus; the six-reader verification findings live only in conversation, which the decision register's own preamble forbids and which makes the citations unauditable.
objections.evidence: grep -rn 'V2TOPIC-F' docs/ returns hits only inside docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md itself. COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md's preamble: 'nothing decided under delegation lives only in conversation.' This reviewer could not verify what V2TOPIC-F-04's DR-117 widening actually says, because no artifact records it.
objections.proposedFix: Land the six-reader register-verification findings as a digest-pinned artifact in docs/coop/artifacts/ before D-001 is adopted, and cite it (path + sha256) from D-001.

objections.claim: The DR-001 route labels the re-record 'mechanical' and sequences it at C3, before any re-review lands — re-recording SATISFIED without independent review, the very defect D-001 itself flags in the existing disposition.
objections.evidence: File 08's status vocabulary: 'SATISFIED — exact acceptance evidence is linked and independently reviewed.' D-001 flags 'the 2026-08-12 SATISFIED was coordinator-recorded without independent review' and routes the audit to DR-204's re-review — but the staged commit plan places C3 ('DR-001 baseline refresh @ HEAD') before C5..C9 (the re-review dispositions). Between C3 and DR-204's landing, the register would again carry a coordinator-recorded SATISFIED with no independent review. Same defect for the 'mechanical' label on R14: reconciling a V1 artifact's stale cross-artifact note edits V1 surface bytes, which route A itself defines as author → independent review → apply.
objections.proposedFix: Either dispatch an independent review of the refreshed DR-001 evidence as part of C3, or record the refresh under a status that does not claim SATISFIED until DR-204 adjudicates. Strike 'mechanical' wherever the act still requires the coop process's review step (DR-001 re-record, R14).

objections.claim: The DR-003 route ('apply reviewed v10-disposition.v4, PASS 0 blocking') cannot close DR-003; presented as the row's closure route, it overstates.
objections.evidence: v10-disposition.v4.review-independent.json (8c1d8893…): decision PASS, blockingFindings 0 — D-001's figures are accurate — but the same verdict states the artifact 'ADJUDICATES NOTHING', counts '3 assessed / 1 discharged / 1 not discharged / 1 partially discharged', leaves $.requiredResolutionAssessment[2].status byte-identical at 'NOT DISCHARGED', keeps sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, and calls the new grade 'strictly weaker than the one it replaces'. DR-003's acceptance cell requires 'Reviewed closure of V10/custody and G19, publication block satisfied by required demonstration, final disposition.' Applying v4 is a lawful step; it is not a route to SATISFIED.
objections.proposedFix: Recast DR-003's entry as a two-stage route: (1) apply reviewed v10-disposition.v4 as the current lawful step; (2) name the remaining closure work (the not-discharged and partially-discharged items, the G19 demonstration, the final disposition) as explicitly still open under DR-003/DR-005.

objections.claim: D-002 is not as free as §2 claims: two of its six listed dimensions are already register-constrained, so the dispatch as framed invites re-litigating recorded product boundaries inside a slice decision.
objections.evidence: 'The first blueprint slice' is indeed defined nowhere (verified: referenced in files 07 L151, 08, 10 L18/L34; no definition in docs/v2 or docs/coop — D-001's measurement holds). But 'TUI in/out' is bounded: DR-123 is a hard blocker for EVERY first slice, 'not conditional on TUI scope', and DR-129 permits TUI only as a host-owned projection that 'cannot replace or package the CLI'. 'Third-party scope' is pre-decided for MVP: DR-128 DEFERRED POST-MVP ('MVP permits first-party/explicitly trusted components... public marketplace/untrusted native/WASM/imperative/network-granted roles stay excluded') and file 10 lists marketplace/ecosystem as excluded 'until product successor'. Calling the selection 'the purest preference-laden decision' across all six dimensions overstates the open space.
objections.proposedFix: In §2, split the dimension list into genuinely open (commands within the mandatory CLI baseline, language roles, closures, statefulness) versus register-bounded (TUI: add-on projection or absent; third-party: fixed at first-party/trusted for MVP absent a DR-010/117 successor), and instruct the D-002 dispatch to treat the bounded ones as constraints, not choices.

objections.claim: Register additions fall outside the adopted checklist's frozen quantifiers, and D-001 does not say whether they bind 'completed' — so the 'complete and only' definition is ambiguous the moment C4 lands.
objections.evidence: Conditions 1 and 2 quantify over DR-001..DR-011 and DR-101..DR-127 exactly. V2TOPIC-F-02's new transition-contract DR row would be numbered outside both ranges; nothing in D-001 states whether completion then requires it. (DR-011's subledger has an explicit new-row binding rule — 'A new matrix residual must be assigned a new row before DR-011 is reconsidered' — the main table has none.) Symptom of the same untracked quantifier: §3's condition-2 routing includes DR-128 and DR-129, which are outside condition 2's DR-101..127 range.
objections.proposedFix: Add one sentence to §1: whether rows added to the register after adoption bind completion (recommended: yes for rows added under condition-1/2 subject areas, recorded per-row), and note that DR-128/129 are routed for completeness even though condition 2 does not quantify over them.

objections.claim: The §3.1 item-4 route choice is simultaneously pre-selected in §3 and parked as an open preference in §4.
objections.evidence: §3's DR-002 route bakes in route (b): 'evidence.v11 disposing EV10-IR-01..03, carrying sealedCapabilityContract/availabilityDifferential — the recorded route (b)... route (a), a retention v29 restore, is the contestable alternative.' §4 then lists 'the item-4 route choice (a vs b)' among decisions made only via D-000 adversarial consensus. If (a) wins that consensus, §3's DR-002 route text is wrong as adopted.
objections.proposedFix: Make the DR-002 route conditional: 'AC-1 successor disposing EV10-IR-01..03; carries the item-4 suppliers IF route (b) is adopted under §4, else a v29 restore runs in parallel.'

objections.claim: Naming the DR-002 successor 'evidence.v11' recreates the exact naming trap file 08 records 'so it is not repeated'.
objections.evidence: check-evidence-v11.py already exists and its subject IS evidence.v10.json (file 08, DR-002 acceptance note: 'the version number is the checker's own — the same trap as check-r1-v1.7.py'). A future evidence.v11.json alongside check-evidence-v11.py-which-checks-v10 is the collision the note warns about.
objections.proposedFix: Either rename/supersede the checker together with the successor, or add a one-line collision notice to the route.

objections.claim: Systemic: §3 pins live candidate heads by version+digest inside a decision text, the citation form file 08's own pin-move record calls 'a known defect' — and it went stale within one commit during this very review.
objections.evidence: Freeze §7.10 (as recited by the pin-move record): pin a property, not a current value. Demonstrated twice in this review cycle: (a) the EIR head moved v9→v10 (ADV-D001-02) between D-001's synthesis HEAD 0ada5b3 and the next commit 4cfd9d4; (b) the freeze digest chain across commits is 6dc7250c → 010f9b11 → c4560fc3 → e4797f47 with the pin-move record's 4314af9e appearing in NO commit. Every §3 route that names a version will need re-verification at execution time anyway; the version pins add staleness risk without adding authority.
objections.proposedFix: State once in §3 that routes bind to the process and the row's acceptance property, with version/digest mentions as non-binding snapshots 'as of HEAD 0ada5b3'.
